tables.label: Table 1
tables.caption: Combination index (CI) and fold of enhancement for inhibiting MERS-CoV pseudovirus infection by HR2P-M2 (μM) and m336 (nM) tested in combination.
footnotes: Note: Each sample was tested in triplicate, and the mean values are presented. Ratio of molar concentration of HR2P-M2 and m336 in combination is 10,000:1.

tables.label: Table 2
tables.caption: Combination index and fold of enhancement for inhibiting MERS-CoV S protein-mediated cell–cell fusion by the HR2P-M2/m336 combination.
footnotes: Note: Each sample was tested in triplicate, and the mean values are presented. The molar concentration ratio of HR2P-M2 and m336 in combination is 4500:1.

tables.label: Table 3
tables.caption: Sensitivity of MERS-CoV pseudoviruses with or without mutations in the receptor-binding domain (RBD) to the inhibitory activity of m336 (nM) and HR2P-M2 (μM) separately.
footnotes: Note: Each sample was tested in triplicate. Data are presented as means ± SD. Resistance ratio (RR50) values are based on IC50 of a mutant strain divided by IC50 of the wild-type stain. The significance of the difference between a mutant strain and the wild-type strain was statistically analyzed by a two-tailed unpaired Student’s t-test using GraphPad Prism, version 5.0. Values with p < 0.05 and p < 0.01 were considered statistically significant and very significant, respectively.

tables.label: Table 4
tables.caption: Combination index and fold of enhancement for inhibiting MERS-CoV pseudoviruses with or without mutations in RBD in S1 subunit and HR1 in S2 subunit of MERS-CoV S protein by HR2P-M2 and m336.
footnotes: Note: The molar concentration ratio of HR2P-M2 and m336 in combination against wildtype virus, viruses with mutations in RBD, and those in HR1 is 10,000:1, 4500:1, and 10,000:1, respectively.
